subject.title: iOS/macOS app cannot connect to a Gateway behind a Basic-auth reverse proxy

question: Should macOS adopt the same arbitrary per-gateway custom-header contract that iOS and Android now use, or should macOS proxy auth be narrowed or split before implementation?
rationale: The remaining gap is clear, but the macOS storage/UI/session boundary determines how credential headers are persisted, cleared, redacted, and applied before Gateway auth; automation should not choose that product/security contract alone.

options.title: Implement macOS parity
options.body: Use the iOS/Android contract as the template and require secure storage, TLS-only header delivery, reset cleanup, redaction, tests, and live proxy proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Split a narrower macOS design
options.body: Keep this issue open but file or sponsor a narrower macOS-only design if arbitrary headers are too broad for the current macOS app architecture.

options.title: Declare macOS out of scope
options.body: Close only if maintainers intentionally decide macOS should not support reverse-proxy credential headers and document the supported alternatives.

recommendation.title: Implement macOS parity
recommendation.body: Use the iOS/Android contract as the template and require secure storage, TLS-only header delivery, reset cleanup, redaction, tests, and live proxy proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the landed iOS path and explicitly identified macOS parity as the remaining scope in the issue thread.
